name: Record alert disposition and define the anomaly-to-event threshold
description: Require a recorded analyst, disposition, and basis for every alert, document what makes an anomaly a security event, and export the population unfiltered.

steps.action: Define alert severities and an analysis timeframe for each, set from measured capacity rather than aspiration.
Assign a named responder or on-call rotation so responsibility is attributable.
Require a recorded disposition and its basis on every alert, replacing bare status changes.
Document the criteria that turn an anomaly into a security event, and reference them from the disposition.
Document any auto-closure suppression rules and their rationale.
Export the unfiltered alert population as the standing evidence artifact.
Tune noisy rules rather than accepting a backlog the responder population cannot process.

implementation_considerations: Demanding written justification on every low-severity alert collapses under volume. Tune detection and document suppression rules instead.
An unfiltered export will reveal a backlog. That visibility is the point and is better found internally than in fieldwork.
Where analysis genuinely happens in a ticketing system, the fix may be reconciling two records rather than changing any behaviour.
typical_duration: Weeks to implement; one period to accumulate the evidence.
prerequisites: An alerting platform capable of exporting the full population

verification_method.how: Export the unfiltered alert population for a completed interval and confirm each item has an analyst, a disposition with a basis, and an analysis time measurable against the committed timeframe.

residual_risk_note: Recorded dispositions show alerts were assessed, not that the assessments were correct; detection quality remains outside what this proves.
period_limitation_note: Dispositions cannot be written retrospectively. Where alerts during an elapsed period have no record, that gap stands.
notes: Deliberately parallel to REM-ENDPOINT-002, which covers the malware-specific detection queue. Apply one, not both, to the same records.
